speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: asked the Minister for Health whether the Ministry will provide cards or letters to Singaporeans who, for medical reasons, are unable to receive their COVID-19 vaccinations, for them to show merchants and their staff who may disallow those without vaccination from entering their stores in future.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: asked the Minister for Health whether a digital vaccine passport system will be used to enable local residents who have been vaccinated to return to pre-COVID-19 activities and be exempted from quarantine upon return from overseas.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: asked the Minister for Health whether the approval of certain less commonly recognised COVID-19 vaccines for use in Singapore may compromise the value of our COVID-19 vaccine certification passport for travel to countries that do not recognise these vaccines.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: asked the Minister for Health whether he can elaborate on the COVID-19 vaccination passport plan, especially on how business, compassionate and leisure travels may be allowed under such a plan.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Other vaccines may be available in the future for those who are not currently medically eligible.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We will continue to evaluate scientific data and review the eligibility criteria accordingly.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Data on the duration of the vaccine’s protection and its effectiveness in preventing transmission, has been encouraging thus far.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: However, most countries have only just started vaccinations.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We will provide further updates when there is significant progress.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: MOH encourages everyone who is medically eligible to get vaccinated.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: The federal authorities in the US have updated travel guidelines for fully vaccinated people.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention have declared that vaccinated travellers do not need a COVID-19 test unless required by the destination country and do not need to be quarantined upon returning to the US but should only be tested before boarding their return flight.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Similarly, the same set of information has allowed us to make changes to the rostered routine testing for some personnel.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, the short answer to the Member's question is yes.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: I am just wondering, very quickly, does the vaccine passport recognition influence our decision to approve specific types of vaccines?

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: So, the concern, of course, is that, if we are approving vaccines with much lower efficacy rates, that will affect the overall recognition of our vaccine passports when they are to be issued.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: And related to that, would the acceleration of the vaccine passport recognition be possible for countries that are deploying comparable vaccines to us?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The factors taken into account for approving the vaccine are the vaccine's quality, its safety and its efficacy.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: While we need to wait for this to develop because the vaccination programmes are still happening in many countries, can I check how many countries are we actively in discussion with?

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Are they mostly unique system of bilateral recognition?

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: And are we expecting a significant public budget to have to be invested, when countries open up more for such a recognition system to happen for air travel?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: It would be premature to discuss the details of this at this point in time.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: As I have explained in my initial answer, the process is very early.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Many countries have not really gotten significant proportion of their population vaccinated.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: And in truth, we are only getting going recently, and so, it is something that we will update as and when we have further information in the future.
